Everything in one place

A workspace, not just a clipboard.

Automatic clipboard history

Opt-in history for text and images, with duplicate suppression. Copy anything, then send it back to the clipboard in one click.

Search that finds it all

Search titles, content, tags — and the words inside images, thanks to on-device OCR. The detail you half-remember is never lost.

Organize your keepers

Favorites, folders, tags and grouped sessions keep projects tidy. Protected favorites stay safe while history rolls on.

Crop, draw, pin

Crop or annotate a screenshot as a new clip, then pin a visual reference above other windows while you work.

Snippets with variables

Save your good replies as reusable snippets with {{variables}}, or capture straight into a rich note with headings and code blocks.

Encrypted when you want it

Optional AES-256 workspace encryption, lock mode, and password-protected backups you can merge back in later.

Alt+S Your workspace, within reach.

Your device. Your call.

A private place for everyday things.

SnapNote works locally. No account, no cloud sync, no telemetry — the app makes no network requests at all.

Capture on your terms

New workspaces start paused. Turn history on when it helps, and pause before copying anything sensitive.

Encryption is optional

Choose a password to encrypt your stored workspace with AES-256. Locking hides it; there is no password recovery, so keep it safe.

Backups you control

Export a backup — plain or password-encrypted JSON — and import it later to merge saved content into a new workspace.

Good to know

Questions, answered.

What to expect before you install.

Read the full desktop guide ↗
Which computers can run SnapNote?+

The v1.2.0 download is for Windows 10 and 11 on x64. The build pipeline is validated on Windows and Linux. A macOS build has not been validated for this preview.

Can I use it without an internet connection?+

Yes. Clipboard history, search, notes, image tools and backups all work locally, and the app never phones home. The only online step may be the installer fetching Microsoft WebView2 if your PC is missing it.

How does text extraction from images work?+

SnapNote uses Tesseract on your device. Install Tesseract and its language data, add it to your PATH, and restart SnapNote — then pick an image and choose Extract text. The installer does not bundle Tesseract. Tesseract installation guide ↗

Is my workspace encrypted automatically?+

No — it is an opt-in feature under Settings & privacy. Backups have their own optional password. Locking hides the workspace and pins; it does not erase your operating system clipboard.

Will it keep my existing SnapNote notes?+

The app reuses the original identity and migrates legacy notes into the new workspace, keeping a recovery copy. Rich formatting, image paste and the old shortcuts still work. Export a backup before a big upgrade anyway — it is one click.

Does it sync between devices?+

Sync is not available in this preview. Everything stays on this device; export and import backups to move content yourself. Optional sync is a possible later step.
